speech_bubble.desc: Head-anchored bubble with typewriter reveal, word wrap, edge clamping/flip and auto-dismiss tied to the talking state

api.desc: POST /emote, /speak, /clear_speech, GET /speech; page reports talking/speech so the API stays truthful

build_verify.desc: cargo check/build clean; verified blinking, emote revert, speak lifecycle with auto-dismiss, clear_speech, edge clamping

keyframe_animations.desc: Stage 2.5 custom keyframe animation: optional `animations` block on the rig root (duration_ms > 0, t in 0..=1, bone ids verified) validated in models.rs; ui/js/animator.js samples clips with smoothstep easing and composes per-bone deltas into rig.js localRotation/computeWorld; timeline bar in Rig Edit Mode (clip selector, +Clip/Del Clip, duration, loop, play/stop, 0-100% scrubber with keyframe ticks, +Keyframe capture routing canvas drags into the clip pose); POST /animate, POST /animate/stop, GET /animations emit avatar-animate + an `animate` SSE frame; MCP tools avatar_list_animations + avatar_animate (10 tools total). Verified: cargo test 12/12, cargo build clean, tools/verify_docs.py zero drift, tools/mcp_smoke_test.py 75 checks offline and 75 live (clips listed + played), 33 headless animator checks, and a CDP run of the real page (play -> finished -> idle, timeline + keyframe capture)

rig_editor_ux.desc: Five Rig & Animation Editor UX fixes: (1) clip naming — `#anim-name` field next to the selector, +Clip uses it (blank -> `clip 1`, `clip 2`, ...), Enter/blur renames the active clip key in place with toast rejection for blank/duplicate names and keeps it selected (animator.renameClip); (2) editor preview no longer swaps clips — animator.stopPlayback() keeps the clip on Stop and stepAnimation parks the playhead at 0 on a natural end while in rig mode; (3) wheel over a selected/held part rotates the PART (0.05 rad/tick, 4-dp snapped) and shift+wheel scales it, bones keep their old wheel behaviour; (4) prominent + Bone in the inspector toolbar working with no selection (child of selection, else of root, else creates root), auto-selects the new bone so its joint+ring highlight; (5) Lock Bone to Part checkbox + Snap Bone to Part button — locked drags move the parent bone and keep the part offset, snap lands the bone on the part and zeroes the offset (persisted as part.lockBone). Verified: 59 headless animator checks, CDP run of the real page for all five fixes (rename/duplicate/blank rejection, finish keeps clip, part wheel 0->8.594deg with bone unchanged, +Bone root_1 auto-selected, locked drag bone pos [0,-60]->[24,-48] with offset unchanged, snap bone world -> old part world with sprite unmoved), lockBone round-trips through Save rig, cargo test 12/12, cargo build embeds ui/, verify_docs + mcp_smoke_test clean

locked_part_drag_fix.desc: Bug: mouse drags did not move the bone of a locked part. Root cause: hitTest gave the selected bone's rotation ring priority, and the ring sits at the bone tip — which for limb sprites is INSIDE the artwork — so pressing the far end of the sprite started a rotate drag and the bone never translated. Fix: partAt() picks the topmost part box first, and a part that is locked (or already selected) owns the press ahead of the ring/joint tests; a locked part also hands the wheel to its bone (wheel rotates/scales the bone, unlocked parts keep their own rotation/scale). Verified with trusted CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent on the real page: press on the ring spot inside arm_r_img -> drag.kind=part, bone pos +30/+15 exactly matching the cursor, rotation unchanged, part offset unchanged, 1:1 per-step tracking (243,97 -> 253,102 -> 263,107 -> 273,112); unlocked sprite still drags its offset; wheel locked -> bone rot 0.5->0.52, unlocked -> part rot 0->0.05; ring outside the artwork still rotates; 10/10 checks plus cargo test 12/12, verify_docs, 59 harness checks, mcp_smoke_test 75

watcher.desc: Stage 3 desktop watcher: `char-rig-watcher.exe` (third binary built by cargo build) subscribes to `GET /events` (reqwest `bytes_stream` + an incremental SSE parser that survives arbitrary chunk boundaries, CRLF and keep-alive comments) and polls `GET /context` on a `tokio::time::interval` (default 20 s, `--context-interval`), firing only on rules loaded from `watcher_rules.json` (`--rules`, built-in defaults when missing): `interaction` double_click/drag_end (15 s cooldown, plain click via `--trigger-single-click`), `window_title` changes matching a case-insensitive keyword, and an `idle_return` when idle drops below the 900 s threshold (both 300 s cooldown). A trigger POSTs an ack `/emote` (default `thinking`, 4000 ms, `--no-ack-emote` disables), POSTs the JSON payload to `--webhook-url`, and spawns `--hermes-cmd` (`CHAR_RIG_HERMES_CMD`) with a one-line prompt carrying {event_type, detail, window_title, idle_secs}; `{prompt}` is substituted or appended as one argv entry with no shell. Exponential-backoff reconnect 1 s -> 30 s; `--dry-run` prints payloads on stdout and touches nothing; diagnostics go to stderr. Verified: cargo build clean (zero warnings, all three exes), cargo test 32/32 watcher + 12/12 lib, a live end-to-end run against a scripted fake avatar API (double_click + drag_end fired, plain click ignored, the duplicate inside the cooldown suppressed, keyword title fired once, idle_return fired, 4 ack emotes received with {expression: thinking, duration_ms: 4000, revert: neutral}, 4 webhook payloads received, 4 Hermes prompts spawned as a single argv entry), and an offline -> online run that reconnected at 1 s then 2 s backoff and then triggered normally; tools/verify_docs.py gained watcher checks (flags, constants, trigger types, watcher_rules.json vs built-in defaults) with zero drift

watcher_single_flight.desc: Watcher dispatch is single-flight and headless: a one-permit Arc<AtomicBool> latch (SingleFlight/FlightGuard, released on Drop) wraps the whole side-effect chain, so a trigger arriving while a --hermes-cmd child (or webhook POST) is still in flight is skipped with a `[watcher] debug: dispatch already in flight` line instead of stacking another hermes process. The child is spawned through tokio::process with stdin(Stdio::null()) (an interactive prompt reads EOF), the wait is wrapped in tokio::time::timeout(--hermes-timeout, default 45 s) and an expired child is start_kill'ed and reaped, and the prompt ends with the headless directive (no follow-up questions; answer with avatar_speak/avatar_emote/avatar_animate/avatar_wave and exit). Verified: cargo test 36/36 watcher (4 new: directive in the prompt, timeout default/parse/rejection, latch admits one dispatch, clones share the latch), cargo build clean for all three exes, and two live runs against a scripted fake avatar API with a probe .bat: 3 triggers 0.25 s apart spawned exactly 1 child and logged 2 skips, and 4 triggers 3 s apart with --hermes-timeout 2 spawned one at a time (each killed at 2 s, permit released so the next spawned), with the prompt argv showing the directive and docs drift zero (DEFAULT_HERMES_TIMEOUT_SECS is now checked by tools/verify_docs.py)

drag_to_move.desc: Play-mode drag-to-move: a press inside avatarBounds() records the grab offset, a move past 8 px turns it into a drag (mode idle, walk segment zeroed, markManual(15) so idle wander stays paused for the gesture and 15 s after), and mousemove follows the cursor 1:1 clamped so the whole art box stays in the viewport; mouseup clears the drag, re-reports drag_end/click/double_click and calls wireRegions(). While dragging, rig.js publishes a full-viewport hit region (the 35 ms cursor tracker would otherwise make the overlay click-through mid-gesture) and bridge.js ignores in-flight avatar-state-changed frames plus bare `walking` echoes that used to snap the avatar to a stale walk target. Verified over CDP against the running app (WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222): 3 consecutive clean runs — sub-threshold press does not move it, a 60/40 px drag moves it exactly 60/40, it parks in idle, the position and bounds survive the release, a drag to the bottom-right clamps to the 1920x1080 box, a plain click does not move it, and Rig Edit Mode still owns the press

watcher_supervision.desc: avatar-desktop now owns the watcher lifecycle: AppCtx gained watcher_child (Mutex<Option<Child>>) and a CHAR_RIG_NO_WATCHER escape hatch (1/true, case- and whitespace-insensitive). After api::start binds and the URL is stored, start_watcher spawns char-rig-watcher{EXE_SUFFIX} from the running exe's directory with --api-url <bound url>, --rules <watcher_rules.json found beside the binaries or up to three dirs up>, stdin(null), inherited stderr, cwd = exe dir and CREATE_NO_WINDOW, then hands the child to a supervisor thread that try_waits it every 250 ms and respawns after a crash (2 s, doubling to 30 s, never during shutdown; the store happens under the same lock request_shutdown takes, so a race cannot orphan a child). request_shutdown (titlebar X, POST /shutdown, RunEvent::ExitRequested|Exit) takes the child, kills and reaps it, logs 'char-rig-watcher stopped', and is idempotent. Verified live: launch -> 'char-rig-watcher rules: C:\hermes\char-rig\watcher_rules.json' + 'started (pid ...)' with cmdline '--rules ... --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8765' and the watcher logging 'dispatch: spawn hermes chat -q (timeout 120s, one at a time)'; taskkill of the watcher -> 'exited (exit code: 1); restarting in 2s' then a new pid exactly 2 s later; POST /shutdown -> 'char-rig-watcher stopped (exit code: 1)' and tasklist shows no watcher and no avatar; CHAR_RIG_NO_WATCHER=1 -> 'not starting char-rig-watcher' and no process. cargo test 18 lib (5 new: NO_WATCHER parsing, binary name, watcher_health, shutdown kill with a pid_alive() check, rules lookup) + 37 watcher, all green; cargo build clean for avatar-desktop + char-rig-watcher, and all three bins compile from a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR (the in-tree char-rig-mcp.exe is held open by the Hermes gateway, so it cannot be relinked in place while that runs); tools/verify_docs.py exits 0

watcher_console.desc: Watcher control panel + pop-out console. Rust: AppCtx owns WatcherState {enabled, child, binary, rules, logs: VecDeque<String> (200)}; watcher_rules_path() now resolves cwd -> beside the binary -> every parent up to models_root().parent(), and the child is pointed at it with --rules. stdout AND stderr are piped into two avatar-watcher-log reader threads that ring-buffer '[HH:MM:SS] line' and echo to the app's stderr (GetLocalTime). New commands get_watcher_status / set_watcher_enabled and routes GET/POST /watcher return {ok, enabled, running, pid, binary_path, rules_path, logs}; every start/stop/log line is also emitted as the watcher-status Tauri event and a watcher SSE frame (event_name() arm added). The supervisor parks while the switch is off. UI: 'Watcher' row in the control panel (#watcher-toggle switch + running/off/missing badge + Logs button) and a floating #watcher-drawer with the live tail, rules_path, Clear and Test ping (notify_interaction double_click); bridge.js owns the state/commands, rig.js publishes the drawer's hit region, DAG unchanged. Verified live over CDP (17 checks green): startup status/rules badge/log tail with timestamps, Logs opens the drawer (430 px region), toggle off (pid gone, badge off, 'stopped' logged) and on (fresh pid), Clear, and Test ping -> the watcher logged 'trigger interaction' and spawned hermes, which called mcp__char_rig__avatar_wave and the avatar waved ('hermes exited with exit code: 0'); GET /watcher returned all 7 keys and POST /watcher false/true stopped and restarted the child with new pids, and POST /shutdown left no watcher behind. cargo test 20 lib (3 new: ring-buffer cap, status keys, rules lookup order) + 37 watcher; cargo build clean for avatar-desktop + char-rig-watcher and all three bins compile from a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR (the Hermes gateway holds the in-tree char-rig-mcp.exe); tools/verify_docs.py exits 0

context_aware_assistant.desc: Turns the avatar from a one-shot reaction into a context-aware assistant. (1) Rich context: desktop_context() now also returns process_name (GetWindowThreadProcessId -> OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) -> QueryFullProcessImageNameW reduced to the exe name, "" on failure/off Windows) and AppCtx keeps a 15-frame VecDeque of emitted SSE frames served as /context's recent_events (EVENT_HISTORY_CAPACITY = 15); GET /clipboard reads CF_UNICODETEXT through a retried OpenClipboard/GlobalLock path, always answers {ok,text,truncated} and caps at MAX_CLIPBOARD_CHARS = 2000 on a char boundary; new MCP tool avatar_get_clipboard and avatar_get_context now reports process_name + a 'type: hint' summary of the recent events. (2) Quick reply: #speech gained an #speech-bubble wrapper with an optional #speech-reply input (hidden until hover/click, Enter sends, Esc dismisses), speech.js owns openReply/closeReply/toggleReply and suspends the bubble's hold timer while it is open, rig.js::wireRegions publishes the bubble's box so the input is clickable over the click-through desktop, and submitting calls the new notify_reply command (POST /reply twin) which broadcasts a user_reply frame and dismisses the bubble. (3) Watcher: handle_frame now routes user_reply (no cooldown, user text quoted into the prompt) and alert (alerts.enabled + alerts.cooldown_secs, default 60 s) alongside interaction; watcher_rules.json gained app_rules [{process, title_contains, animation, prompt_hint}] and alerts, both optional so the old schema still parses; a matched app rule supplies the ack (expression -> /emote, any other name -> /animate clip) and a 'Context:' prompt hint, and hermes_cmd keeps one conversation across triggers (`hermes chat --continue char-rig --create-if-missing -Q -q`: -c resumes/creates the named session, -Q keeps the banner out of the log, -q stays last because the prompt is the final argv entry). POST /alert validates source/summary/severity(info|warn|error) and broadcasts an alert frame. (4) HEADLESS_DIRECTIVE now documents avatar_get_clipboard/process_name, invites chaining several tool calls in one turn, and caps the bubble at 180 characters. Verified live: /context returned process_name Hermes.exe + recent_events, /clipboard returned the real 2000-char-capped clipboard, POST /reply and /alert produced user_reply/alert frames on a curl -N SSE stream (blank reply and severity "loud" rejected with the documented 400 bodies); a scripted fake avatar API drove the watcher end-to-end (dry-run printed all five trigger types, the app-rule trigger carried animation=alert + prompt_hint, live mode posted /emote acks + /animate {name:alert,loop:true} + webhook payloads); CDP on the real page clicked the bubble, typed with trusted key events, pressed Enter and saw the bubble hide, input empty, toast 'Reply sent' while notify_reply reached Rust; a Node harness imported the shipped rig.js and proved wireRegions publishes the bubble box only while visible; cargo test --lib --bins 27 lib + 48 watcher green (cargo test alone exits 1 at the doctest stage because this toolchain ships no rustdoc), tools/mcp_smoke_test.py 86 checks green against the new bridge built in a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR (the gateway holds the in-tree char-rig-mcp.exe), and tools/verify_docs.py exits 0 with the new route/event/tool/app_rules checks

command_bar_and_sessions.desc: Desktop command bar + session reset. (1) Ask/task anywhere: a floating #command-bar anchored under the avatar (speech.js positionCommandBar, re-anchored every 250 ms while open) opens from Enter or '/', the new titlebar chat icon, the control panel's Ask… button or a click on the speech bubble; it focuses #command-input immediately, publishes its own hit region through rig.js::wireRegions (verified in a Node harness importing the shipped rig.js: closed -> not published, open -> published) and Esc closes it back to click-through. The bubble's hold timer is now paused while it is hovered, the quick-reply box is pinned, or the reply/command input has focus. (2) quick_tasks chips: lib.rs::quick_tasks reads [{label,prompt}] out of watcher_rules.json (blank entries skipped, MAX_QUICK_TASKS=6, three built-in defaults on missing/unreadable file), GET /watcher returns them, bridge.js mirrors them into watcher.quickTasks and main.js renders them as chips; a click sends the prompt and closes the bar. (3) New chat: the bar's ↺, the control panel's New chat and POST /session/reset all broadcast session_reset (do_session_reset + reset_session command); the app owns no session state. char-rig-watcher.exe keeps a SessionState (id/turns/last_turn/seed/counter) and substitutes {session} in hermes_cmd at spawn time; session_reset rotates it, max_session_turns / session_idle_reset_secs rotate automatically, session_base sets the prefix, and a template without {session} logs a startup warning. (4) Thinking feedback: submitting shows a 'Thinking…' card + the thinking face immediately (beginThinking/showThinking; the speech-clear Rust emits for the old prompt is turned into the card, and a thinking card deliberately ignores stray clears so a late event cannot blank it); a real avatar_speak replaces it. user_reply prompts now say the user typed it directly in the desktop overlay and is waiting, so the model treats it as a task and reports back with avatar_speak. Verified: cargo test --lib --bins 32 lib + 58 watcher green (new: session ids/rotation, {session} substitution, reset-frame rotation without a trigger, max-turns + idle rotation, quick_tasks parse/fallback/cap, session_reset frame + bubble dismissal, direct-task prompt); tools/verify_docs.py exits 0 with new quick_tasks/{session} checks; CDP against the real page: Enter opens + focuses, chips are the four rules-file labels, Esc closes, '/' reopens, typing + Enter sends (bar closes, thinking card appears, expression=thinking), New chat dismisses it and /context's recent_events shows user_reply then session_reset, and an avatar_speak replaces the thinking card; watcher e2e against a scripted fake API with an argv probe: spawn 1 used --continue char-rig-<seed>, session_reset rotated it to -2 and spawn 2 used the new id, max_session_turns=1 rotated between two triggers, prompt always last in argv

life_signs_polish.desc: Bubble re-anchored to the head every animation frame (anchor gap held at 29.6-30.2 px while the avatar walked 903->988 px) and the avatar stands still while a bubble is up (2 s past nextIdle without moving, wanders again once it closes); text-driven lip sync per revealed character (open/flat/closed sprite variants + eased procedural openness); pupils follow the pointer and the focused command bar, clamped to +-4 px (pixel centroid moved 5.71 px between far-left and far-right aim while the hand sprite moved 0.00), with idle glances every 2-4 s; hover eases a ~3 deg head tilt (head joint -0.0052 -> 0.0562 rad); legacy prototype dirs deleted

window_border_perch.desc: Stage 4 window-border awareness + avatar_perch. Rust: desktop_context() now also returns window_rect (DwmGetWindowAttribute DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS with a GetWindowRect fallback) and visible_windows (EnumWindows, z-order, keeping visible/non-minimized/non-cloaked/titled windows owned by another process, capped at MAX_VISIBLE_WINDOWS = 5), both converted physical px -> CSS px with GetDpiForSystem()/96 (primary monitor scale) so they match the WebView2 overlay; degenerate rects (minimized windows: 0x0 at -32000) are dropped. New POST /perch {edge, window_process?, offset?}: resolves the rect from a case-insensitive substring of a visible window's process_name (else the foreground window_rect), converts edge + the artwork's extents around its root (AvatarBounds {left,right,up,down}, reported by the page through report_state -- the root sits near the hips, so half the height left the feet floating) + offset into a target, clamps it to primary_viewport(), marks the state perched with perch_rect and publishes a `state` frame; 400 {ok:false,error} for an unknown edge, an unmatched process (naming the visible ones) or no focused window. POST /move gained an optional look_at [x,y]; /move, POST /state, a drag and W/C all clear the perch. Page: avatar.perched/perchRect/lookAt in state.js, adopted from every state frame in bridge.js (which also reports the art extents), idle wander paused and the gaze pinned to the perch rect's centre in main.js; __avatarDebug.perched() added. MCP: 13th tool avatar_perch (edge validated locally against PERCH_EDGES before any HTTP call), avatar_move look_at (validated locally), avatar_get_context now summarises window_rect + visible_windows (as `Code.exe@(400, 300) 800x500 | ...`) and the perched flag; the watcher's HEADLESS_DIRECTIVE documents avatar_perch and the new context fields. Docs: README (thirteen tools, /perch examples), API.md (POST /perch, GET /context shape, state fields, MCP table), ARCHITECTURE.md (33 routes, 13 tools, state flow, limitations) and verify_docs.py's pinned counts. Verified: cargo test --lib --bins 52 lib + 8 mcp + 64 watcher green (new: rect conversion + degenerate rejection, edge parse/reject, feet-on-edge/offset/clamp math, asymmetric extents, bounds sanitisation, state serialisation, PerchBody parsing, edge validation, visible-window resolution incl. the 400 message, MoveBody look_at, tool schema/dispatch/local validation/look_at/context summary); cargo build --bins clean for all three exes; tools/verify_docs.py 33 routes / 13 tools zero drift; tools/mcp_smoke_test.py 97 checks offline and 119 live; live API run against real windows: /context returned window_rect (146,67,1692,909) for Hermes.exe plus 5 visible windows, perch top_left on WindowsTerminal (290,244,1115,628) landed the art's bottom edge exactly on y=244 and its left edge on x=290, left put the art's right edge on the window border (root 220), right targeted 1475, bottom clamped to 1010 so the art stayed on screen, offset 80 moved the target to 440, and both error paths returned 400 with actionable messages; the avatar then held still for 9 s while perched (idle wander paused), aimed its gaze at the rect centre (1252,451), and a POST /move cleared perched while look_at set the gaze to (1500,300); POST /state, a trusted CDP drag and the W key each cleared the perch (perched:false, perch_rect:null).

import_folder_copy_fix.desc: Bug: `import_model` copied the manifest's ENTIRE parent folder into models/<slug>/, so importing a standalone model.json that sat in Downloads/ or on the Desktop recursively copied the user's whole folder (installers, personal files, gigabytes) and could take minutes. Fix: the copy set is now exactly the rig's referenced assets -- `part_images(&rig)` (part.image plus every part.variants entry) resolved and validated by `inline_images`, so absolute paths, `..` traversal, missing files and >16 MB sprites still fail before anything is written -- each copied to the same relative path, plus the normalised model.json; `copy_tree` (the recursive folder mirror) is deleted and the source folder is never walked. Verified: two new unit tests in models.rs -- `import_copies_only_the_referenced_sprites` builds a fake Downloads/ containing model.json + 3 referenced sprites (one only reachable through variants) + setup.exe + notes.txt + parts/unused.png + unrelated/holiday.png, imports it, and asserts the 3 sprites are byte-identical at their relative paths while every unrelated file/folder is absent AND load_model() resolves all 3 images from the copy; `import_rejects_traversal_without_writing_a_model` asserts `../secret.png` fails with no half-built folder left behind. cargo test --lib --bins 54 lib + 8 mcp + 64 watcher green; all three binaries build clean from a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR (the in-tree exes were held open by the running avatar/watcher and the gateway); tools/verify_docs.py exit 0; tools/mcp_smoke_test.py 97 checks (offline branch, isError paths untouched). Docs updated: MODEL_FORMAT.md (accepted-formats table + a selective-import paragraph) and API.md's POST /import notes.

deferred_mcp_tool_search_recovery.desc: Root cause: Hermes defers MCP server tools per session, so HEADLESS_DIRECTIVE told the model to call mcp__char_rig__avatar_* straight away and a local model on a new/resumed session looped on 'deferred tools must be invoked through tool_call by the exact name tool_search returns' until --hermes-timeout killed it, leaving the overlay on a permanent Thinking... card. Fix, three layers: (1) HEADLESS_DIRECTIVE now leads with 'FIRST TOOL CALL IN THIS SESSION: the char-rig tools are DEFERRED MCP tools' and instructs tool_search(query="avatar_") (or "char-rig") once, then tool_call with the exact names it returns, before the existing signature list; (2) char-rig-watcher.rs classifies every dispatch with a RunOutcome {Succeeded, Failed, TimedOut, WaitFailed, SpawnFailed} and, for anything but a clean exit 0, posts the fallback bubble POST /speak {"text":"Sorry, I hit a snag or timed out.","expression":"sad","duration_ms":4000} from inside the child's task (before the FlightGuard drops, so it lands ahead of a queued trigger), spawn_hermes became an async fn taking the reqwest client + api_url; (3) ui/js/speech.js keeps a THINKING_TIMEOUT_MS (125 s) timer armed by beginThinking/showThinking and cleared by speak/hideSpeechNow/endThinking, which clears a stuck card, reverts the expression to neutral and toasts. Verified: cargo test --lib --bins 54 lib + 8 mcp + 69 watcher green (5 new watcher tests: the tool_search hint exists and precedes the first signature with underscore tool names; fallback_speech_for fires only for non-clean outcomes with exactly the three /speak keys and a real expression; a captured raw POST /speak from deliver_fallback; nothing posted for Succeeded; and a real 'python -c sleep(30)' child killed at --hermes-timeout 1 s that still posts the bubble and releases the single-flight permit). tools/verify_docs.py exit 0 and tools/mcp_smoke_test.py 97 checks pass offline; both UI-embedded binaries rebuilt.

stage5_ai_profiles.desc: Stage 5: AI model/backend switching, pure Rust. watcher_rules.json grew `active_profile` + `ai_profiles` (tagged `openai_compat` / `hermes_cli`); char-rig-watcher.rs gained an `InferenceBackend` trait (boxed-future `dispatch`) with `OpenaiCompatBackend` (one POST to the server's chat-completions path with response_format json_object, reply `{speech, expression?, perch_edge?, window_process?, details?, escalate?}` parsed by `AiReply::parse` and applied as /perch -> /emote -> /speak, bubble cut to 180 chars, details forwarded, sad fallback bubble on failure, `escalate:true` handing off to the hermes_cli profile) and `HermesCliBackend` (the old spawn_hermes runner), plus `AiRuntime`/`AiShared` which re-read the rules file on an `ai_profile` SSE frame so a switch lands on the next trigger with no restart and no rebuild; `app_rules[].profile` and `quick_tasks[].profile` pin one trigger to a brain (the chip's profile rides in the user_reply frame); the no-tools prompt path is Trigger::brief (no CLI directive, so the MCP tool names never reach a model that has no tools) and inlines a fresh GET /context snapshot, reading GET /clipboard only when the user's words mention it (mentions_clipboard) — verified live that an unrelated question does not contain the clipboard marker while a clipboard question does. lib.rs/api.rs added GET /ai-profiles ({ok, active_profile, active_health{reachable,status,detail}, profiles[]} with an 800 ms /health -> /v1/models probe, `cli` + PATH lookup for the agent), POST /ai-profile (validate -> atomic write-rules-and-rename -> probe -> `ai_profile` SSE frame + `ai-profile-changed` event, 400 listing valid names) and the get_ai_profiles / set_ai_profile Tauri commands; the panel gained an AI Brain row (label dropdown + online/offline/cli dot, refreshed every 12 s); char-rig-mcp.rs added the 14th tool avatar_switch_ai and reports active_profile + ai_profiles + active_health from avatar_get_context. Tests: lib 67, mcp 12, watcher 86 (new: tagged-schema parsing, legacy-profile synthesis, active/override resolution, escalate target, reply parse/action-order/truncation, chat_url normalisation, request body contract, a captured fake chat-completions -> perch/emote/speak run, dead-endpoint fallback, escalating report, ai_profile reload, health probe + atomic profile persistence + PATH lookup, avatar_switch_ai schema/validation). tools/verify_docs.py extended to validate the ai_profiles block and updated to 35 routes / 36 commands / 15 event types / 14 MCP tools; tools/mcp_smoke_test.py covers avatar_switch_ai offline + live.

stage5_native_gestures.desc: Stage 5 extension: native avatar gestures from local `openai_compat` models, no hermes_cli escalation. `AiReply` gained `animate?` (a clip name from the rig's own GET /animations list; trimmed, blank ignored, case kept) and `wave?` (bool); `AvatarAction` gained `Wave` -> POST /wave (empty body) and `Animate{name}` -> POST /animate {"name": name, "loop": false}. `actions_with_clips(&clips)` orders perch -> emote -> gesture -> speak so the gesture plays while the bubble types; `wave: true` outranks `animate`, and `animate: "wave"` becomes the built-in Wave unless the rig lists its own `wave` clip (case-insensitive `has_clip`), so sprite and procedural models both gesture. Execution swallows failures like the other actions and a rig that rejects /animate for the wave clip degrades to POST /wave instead of losing the gesture or the /speak. The no-tools prompt inlines `Animation clips on this rig: ...` from GET /animations (fetched alongside the prompt so the decision needs no second request) and AI_REPLY_CONTRACT documents the animate/wave keys; lfm3-fast's system_prompt asks for gestures and keeps escalate strictly for multi-step or external-tool work (clipboard, network scan, files, terminal). Tests: watcher 92 (new: animate/wave parsing incl. blank, wrong type and case; gesture-before-speech ordering; wave-outranks-animate; animate:"wave" with and without a custom clip; a real POST /wave; a real POST /animate {"name":"dance","loop":false}; and a 400-rejected clip falling back to /wave without swallowing /speak), with the fake-server helper generalised to serve_responses(status, body). Verified live: wave:true drove state "waving", and animate:"dance" was rejected 400 by the real API, swallowed, with the bubble still spoken.

overlay_ux_fixes.desc: Overlay UX fixes. (1) The "Thinking…" card now covers the watcher's own triggers, not just the command bar: `bridge.js` turns an `emote` with `expression: "thinking"` into `speech.showThinkingForAck()`, which defers to an answer already on screen (`speech.visible && !speech.thinking`) and otherwise shows the card + arms `THINKING_TIMEOUT_MS`, so `drag_end`, `idle_return`, `window_title` and `alert` visibly wait. (2) `GET /context` no longer reports the overlay itself: the overlay is a full-screen transparent window that takes foreground the moment the user drags the avatar or clicks a chip, which poisoned the model's context and made an unqualified `POST /perch` target the overlay's own rect. `reported_window` (with `is_self_foreground`: PID == `std::process::id()`, else an exact exe-name match, and a blank self name never matching) falls back to `visible_windows[0]` — already z-ordered and self-filtered — for title, process and rect, or reports a blank context when the overlay is alone. (3) The 1 px Windows 11 frame: `strip_dwm_frame` at setup sets `DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR` (34) to `DWMWA_COLOR_NONE` and `DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE` (33) to `DWMWCP_DONOTROUND` on the main window's HWND, `tauri.conf.json` sets `shadow: false`, and `ui/styles.css` zeroes margin/padding/border/outline/overflow on `html`/`body`/`canvas`. Tests: lib 72 (new: `is_self_foreground` by PID and name, the fallback picking the front-most window and its rect, an ordinary foreground window left untouched, the blank overlay-alone case, and the name fallback when the PID is unreadable). Verified live: with avatar-desktop foreground, `/context` reported Hermes.exe and `POST /perch {"edge":"top_right"}` used that window's rect; a CDP-fired `drag_end` showed the "Thinking…" card and the slow answer replaced it; the corner attribute reads back as 1 and a pixel probe of the left screen edge shows a flat profile with no 1 px line.

local_voice_tts.desc: Goal 1 local Piper TTS. `src-tauri/src/tts.rs` owns it: `TtsConfig` (#[serde(default)] on the container, so a pre-voice rules file still loads) reads enabled / piper_exe_path / model_path / espeak_data_path / speaker_id / length_scale from the `tts` block; a missing piper.exe or .onnx logs one warning, reports ready:false with the reason, and the app keeps running silently. `do_speak` in lib.rs is the single hook, so POST /speak, the `speak` command, MCP avatar_speak and every agent reply are voiced exactly once (the watcher is never hooked separately, which would double-speak). `sanitize_for_speech` strips fenced code, markdown markers, links/URLs, <tags>, emoji and control chars, and an empty result is skipped. One FIFO `avatar-tts` worker thread spawns piper.exe with CREATE_NO_WINDOW, --model, --espeak_data (Windows Piper needs it), optional --speaker/--length_scale and --output_file, writes the cleaned UTF-8 text to stdin, closes it, waits, then plays the temp .wav with PlaySoundW(SND_FILENAME|SND_SYNC|SND_NODEFAULT) and deletes it, so lines queue instead of overlapping and the HTTP/UI threads never block. Control surface: GET/POST /tts, get_tts_status / set_tts_enabled, the tts-status event, and the panel's Voice row (on/muted/missing). Mute is runtime-only and never rewrites watcher_rules.json. Tests: 12 unit tests (config full/partial/legacy/malformed, sanitizing, truncation, path problems, queue-full) plus a live run that produced a 176,428-byte wav and left 0 temp files behind.

local_voice_stt.desc: Goal 2 push-to-talk. `src-tauri/src/stt.rs` owns it: `SttConfig` (#[serde(default)]) reads enabled / hotkey / whisper_exe_path / whisper_model_path / silero_vad_model_path / vad_threshold / language / min_speech_ms; a missing binary, model or microphone logs one warning, reports ready:false and disables PTT gracefully. One `avatar-ptt` thread owns the whole state machine idle→listening→transcribing: it polls GetAsyncKeyState for the hold hotkey, captures through winmm `waveIn` at 16 kHz mono 16-bit (falling back to 48/44.1 kHz mono or stereo), downmixes and linearly resamples to 16 kHz, drops clips under min_speech_ms and caps a hold at 60 s. The clip is written to %TEMP%, handed to whisper-cli.exe (-m -f -l -nt -np --vad --vad-model --vad-threshold) with CREATE_NO_WINDOW, its stdout cleaned of [BLANK_AUDIO]/(music)/[inaudible]/timestamps/control chars, and the wav deleted immediately. A non-empty transcript is POSTed to /reply exactly like typed input (so the watcher wakes and Piper speaks the answer); an empty one sends nothing. Starting a hold calls tts::interrupt() so the mic never hears the avatar. Control surface: GET/POST /stt, get_stt_status / ptt_start / ptt_stop / set_stt_enabled, the stt-status event, and the panel's Hold to talk row with an idle/listening/transcribing/missing badge. Tests: 12 unit tests plus an ignored end-to-end test that runs whisper on a real 16 kHz clip.

local_screen_vision.desc: Goal 3 local screen vision, owned by char-rig-watcher.exe. GET /context now also returns the foreground window's window_rect, and a new `vision` block in watcher_rules.json (#[serde(default)] at container and field level, so pre-vision rules files still load) drives it: enabled, profile_name (a named openai_compat AI profile, resolved with AiRuntime::named so a screenshot never goes to the active text model), capture_mode (active_window | full_screen), max_image_dim (clamped 64-4096), jpeg_quality (clamped 1-100) and trigger_phrases (case/apostrophe/whitespace-insensitive matching against typed or dictated user_reply text). src-tauri/src/bin/capture/mod.rs grabs pixels with GDI GetDC/CreateCompatibleDC/CreateCompatibleBitmap/BitBlt + GetDIBits, clamps the window_rect to the virtual screen, refuses a rect that is the avatar overlay itself (falling back to the primary monitor), downscales with the image crate so max(w,h) <= max_image_dim, JPEG-encodes in memory and base64-encodes a data:image/jpeg;base64 URL - nothing is written to disk. vision_request_body builds one OpenAI-shaped multimodal chat/completions body (system prompt + the JSON reply contract, then [{type:text},{type:image_url}]) with response_format json_object and the profile's max_tokens; a failed capture, a missing profile or a dead endpoint speaks a short apology instead of crashing or blocking text replies. Trigger path: POST /reply gained include_screen (ReplyBody -> do_user_reply_with_profile -> user_reply frame) and quick_tasks chips may carry include_screen; wants_vision fires on that flag or on a phrase match, while routine triggers never capture. UI: the panel's What's on screen? button (#btn-screen) and the matching command-bar chip both send the explicit flag. Tests: 6 new watcher unit tests (defaults, legacy/partial/full_screen config, phrase normalisation, enabled:false + routine triggers, the multimodal body, include_screen on a reply frame).

stage6_visual_audio_spatial_polish.desc: Stage 6 visual, audio & spatial polish. (1) Audio-driven lip sync: after Piper writes its temp wav and before PlaySoundW blocks, tts.rs reads the file back, parses the RIFF chunks (8/16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE), averages the channels per frame, computes the RMS of each 25 ms bucket and normalizes the loudest bucket to 1.0; the payload rides a Tauri `tts-envelope` event emitted right as playback starts, with `tts-envelope-stop` on finish/mute/interrupt(). The worker has no AppHandle, so the app installs one emitter (`set_emitter`) at startup. Silence, a non-PCM wav or a muted voice yields an empty envelope. Frontend: state.js grew an `envelope`/`envelopeBucketMs`/`envelopeAt` trio, speech.js gained setAudioEnvelope/clearAudioEnvelope and updateSpeech indexes the samples by elapsed playback time (falling back to the per-character mouthPoseFor mapping when the voice is muted, missing or done), and bridge.js listens for both events. (2) Live window tether: AvatarState tracks perch_hwnd/perch_edge/perch_offset/perch_bounds (all serde(skip), so the state wire is unchanged); POST /perch stores the resolved HWND via resolve_perch_hwnd (same predicate as the rect resolution, and the reported window's handle when the overlay holds foreground) plus the art bounds frozen at perch time; an `avatar-perch` thread polls every 60 ms with IsWindow/IsIconic/DwmGetWindowAttribute, recomputes the target through the pure perch_update() and publishes a state frame only when it moved more than PERCH_FOLLOW_TOLERANCE (1 px), and on a gone/minimized window clears the perch, sets idle and publishes. Freezing the bounds matters: the live reported extents wobble ~10 px with the walk animation and made the target chase its tail. A new break_perch command (called by the page when a press becomes a drag) and drag_end both clear the perch, so the tracker never fights the pointer; POST /move already did. (3) Multi-monitor virtual desktop: screen_metrics() reads SM_X/Y/CX/CYVIRTUALSCREEN and the CSS scale, setup sizes and positions the overlay to the whole virtual desktop, ScreenMetrics::physical_rect subtracts the origin (so a left-hand monitor maps to positive CSS x), every rect/cursor/visible_windows value goes through it, monitor_bounds_for (MonitorFromPoint + GetMonitorInfoW) clamps perch_target to the monitor the window is on instead of the primary, and capture::rect_from_context converts /context's CSS rect back to physical pixels for the GDI BitBlt. GET /context now also reports foreground_hwnd, per-window hwnd and the `screen` object. (4) Reaction clip library: nod, shake_head, celebrate, alert_ping and idle_fidget added to models/demo-blob and to nebulon-9 (the model the app boots with), so GET /animations lists them and an openai_compat model can send {"animate": "nod"}. Tests: 110 lib (wav envelope shape/normalisation/stereo downmix/8-bit/garbage, screen metrics offsets and DPI, perch follow/lost/tolerance/frozen bounds, state wire) and 107 watcher (+2 capture CSS->physical cases).

global_gaze_and_chat_history.desc: Global eye tracking + in-memory conversation history, plus the §8 doc cleanup. (1) Gaze: spawn_cursor_tracker (lib.rs) now emits the page-local Tauri event `cursor-pos` {x, y} (CSS px of the virtual desktop) from the same 35 ms GetCursorPos poll that drives click-through — throttled by the pure, unit-tested cursor_emit_due (CURSOR_EMIT_DEADBAND = 3.0, CURSOR_EMIT_INTERVAL_MS = 50) and emitted whether or not the window is click-through (only a visible, non-minimized window is required); it never bumps AvatarState.revision and never touches the SSE bus. Frontend: main.js listens for cursor-pos, updateGaze now prioritises look_at > focused command bar > perch_rect > global cursor (4 s after the last move, then idle glances) and derives a damped head-bone yaw bias (<= 0.22 rad) that rig.js::animOffset adds for the head bone, clamped by localRotation against bone.limits; a malformed look_at can no longer poison the smoothing with NaN. (2) History: AppCtx gained chat: Mutex<VecDeque<ChatMessage>> (CHAT_HISTORY_CAPACITY = 50) + chat_seq + an AppHandle slot; push_chat (bounded, emits `chat-message`), chat_history, clear_chat (emits `chat-history-cleared`) and chat_history_json; do_user_reply_with_profile records "user" turns, do_speak records "assistant" ones (details + expression), do_session_reset clears. New get_chat_history command (registered, 44 total) and GET /history (38 routes) share that body. do_speak was split into do_speak_opt(Option<&AppHandle>) so the recording path is testable without a window. UI: ui/js/history.js + a #history-drawer card (panel History button, command-bar ☰, H / Esc), hydrating via get_chat_history, appending from chat-message, emptying on chat-history-cleared, auto-scrolling only when already at the newest turn, per-turn Details/Copy, and a hit region published only while open. (3) build.rs now links tauri-build's resource.lib into the test binaries: without the Common-Controls v6 manifest the lib unit-test harness died before main with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xc0000139) because wry imports comctl32 v6 symbols. (4) Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md §1/§2/§3/§5/§6/§7 updated (commands 44, routes 38, new events/command/route, new History + gaze sections) and §8 now records only real limitations — the stale primary-monitor-only, perch-is-a-point, lip-sync-has-no-audio-analysis and watcher_rules-needs-CHECKOUT bullets were replaced/removed; README (History drawer, global eye tracking, Status) and API.md (GET /history) match; tools/verify_docs.py pins the three new constants and ui CHAT_LIMIT. Tests: 115 lib (5 new: bounded eviction, reply/speak recording, rejected turns, session-reset clearing, cursor throttle) + 12 mcp + 107 watcher + 2 integration; cargo build clean with 0 warnings; verify_docs.py exit 0. Live: GET /history showed the trimmed prompt and the reply with its details; the drawer hydrated/hydrated-empty/live-appended and cleared on POST /session/reset; a real OS click at the drawer's ✕ closed it, proving the hit region; GetCursorPos moves drove gaze.targetX/Y to the cursor (700,250 / 1650,820) with tilt clamped at 0.2199 and a look_at A/B giving +0.2197 / -0.2194, clamped to +0.05 with limits {min:-0.05,max:0.05}.

cross_platform_platform_layer.desc: Cross-platform refactor: one OS boundary + cross-platform audio. (1) New src-tauri/src/platform/ module: types.rs (DesktopContext, WindowRect, VisibleWindow, ScreenMetrics, ClipboardText/Write, ReportedWindow, is_self_foreground, reported_window, truncate_chars, clipboard caps — pure data), hotkey.rs (the "Ctrl+Shift+A" grammar, portable Hotkey{modifiers,vk}, modifier constants; pure and tested on every target), win32.rs (all the Win32/DWM/CF_UNICODETEXT/GetCursorPos/RegisterHotKey code moved out of lib.rs verbatim, now behind a HotkeyListener{register,poll,release} handle) and unix.rs (Linux/macOS: xdotool/wmctrl/xrandr/osascript window probes, xclip/xsel/wl-copy/pbcopy clipboard, rdev for global cursor + held-key state, global-hotkey for the shortcut). lib.rs keeps only portable logic and re-exports the historical paths, so api.rs needs no change. (2) tts.rs playback is rodio (WASAPI/ALSA/PipeWire/CoreAudio via cpal): one OutputStream per worker, a Sink per line with sleep_until_end, and an Arc<Sink> shared with stop_playback so mute/interrupt still cuts a line; PlaySoundW and the Win32_Media_Audio feature are gone. (3) stt.rs capture is cpal instead of winmm waveIn: the default input device at its own format, append_mono downmixes interleaved frames to mono i16 in the callback, the existing 15 ms drain + resample_pcm16 path is unchanged; key polling goes through platform::key_is_down. (4) tools/platform-check/ type-checks the real platform tree for another OS without Tauri/GTK (rdev stubbed via [patch.crates-io] because its x11 build script wants pkg-config). Tests: 123 lib (adds sanitize-before-truncate, "tts": null is absent, enqueue-before-init no-op, append_mono downmix/clamp/partial-frame; the 2 hotkey-grammar tests moved into hotkey.rs), 12 mcp, 107 watcher. Verified: cargo build --bins clean, cargo test --lib --bins all green, cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and --target x86_64-apple-darwin on tools/platform-check both clean (0 warnings), verify_docs.py exit 0. Docs: README "Running on Linux and macOS" + rodio/cpal playback and capture text, ARCHITECTURE platform section, dependency table, thread and function tables, and §8 rewritten to the real limits (Wayland has no window context, screen vision is GDI-only, macOS needs Accessibility).

emberwing_model.desc: New shipped procedural rig models/emberwing (lantern moth): 22 bones, 96 shape parts, four mirrored wings with ember eyespots, segmented abdomen ending in a lantern, feathered antennae, six distinct walk-phase legs, and six clips (flutter/hover/scan/alert/bow/flare). Verified live over CDP + curl: GET /models reports error:null, POST /model loads it, the clip sampler keeps the wings exactly mirrored (wing_u_l == -wing_u_r, tips lagging), the real OS cursor drives gaze tilt 0.08, and a happy expression lights mouth_open/eye_wide/brow_up, so the tagged eye/pupil/head/mouth parts work on a shape-only rig. Wing bones needed limits +-5.2 rad: the pi+0.55 rest angle was clamped to pi by the default limit and made the shipped pose asymmetric.

survival_inventory_fishing.desc: Survival plugin gains a slot-limited inventory and a three-phase fishing mini-game, all inside the Wasm guest. Inventory: plugins/survival/src/inventory.rs holds a 10-item catalog (fish/bait/tool/material/junk, per-item stack_max, emoji icon, edible -> food id) and a fixed-length Vec<Option<Stack>> bag; GET /inventory, POST /inventory/add, /inventory/remove and /inventory/use (item, id or slot; an edible item is eaten through the same SurvivalStats::eat path /survival/feed uses and is spent only when the meal is accepted). Fishing: fishing.rs is a four-phase machine (waiting -> biting -> reeling -> idle) with a hidden bite time, a reaction window anchored on the scheduled bite, and a triangle-wave reel the plugin judges from its own clock, so the page draws the marker but cannot widen the sweet spot; routes are GET /fishing and POST /fishing/cast, /hook, /reel, /cancel, and the events are fishing-started, fishing-bite, fish-hooked, fishing-result and inventory-changed. Verified: 124 guest tests (cargo test --lib, up from 66) plus 148+12+107 app tests pass and tools/verify_docs.py exits 0 with the new schema pins. Live over curl: cast -> poll GET /fishing -> hook -> reel at the computed sweet centre caught a River perch and stored it (inventory 3 -> 4), /context's recent_events carried all five frames in order, POST /inventory/use on the perch moved hunger 40 -> 50 and emptied the slot, and the refusal paths answered 400 (unknown id, gear) / 409 (over-remove, absent item, hook with no line). UI driven in a real browser against the live API: the Bag tab drew 20 slots with icons, counts and blurbs, selection correctly enabled/disabled Use, Add and Use round-tripped, and one in-page cast -> auto-strike -> timed Space press landed a catch (note plus badge 6/20). POST /config with {fishing:{difficulty,hook_key}} applied live (effective_period_ms 1000, effective_sweet_width 0.147) and refused an unknown nested key, a bad range and a bad slot count by name.

survival_store_economy.desc: Survival plugin gains a coin economy and a shop, entirely inside the Wasm guest. model.rs: SurvivalStats carries `coins` (u32, STARTING_COINS = 100), serialized with the rest of the stats, credited/debited through add_coins/try_spend_coins (saturating) and rendered in stats.to_json; the field's serde default is the starting balance, so a state saved before the economy existed upgrades to 100 coins rather than 0 (an explicit 0 is still honoured). store.rs: StoreItem {id,label,icon,buy_price,sell_price,category} + default_catalog() with worm_bait 4/1, glowing_lure 24/10, driftwood 6/3, river_weed 5/2 and fishing_rod 75/30, category bait/material/tool; tests pin that every stocked id is a real inventory item, that the shelf matches the item's kind, and that sell_price < buy_price. routes.rs: GET /store (catalog with owned/stack_max + coins + starting_coins + inventory summary), POST /store/buy and POST /store/sell ({item|id, count} with count 1-99; a non-integer or out-of-range count is a 400, never a clamp). Buy is all-or-nothing: coins and Inventory::room_for (a throwaway-copy probe that runs the real stacking rule) are both checked before anything moves, 409 insufficient_coins / 409 inventory_full, and nothing is charged on a refusal; sell is exact, 409 not_enough_items, 400 for an id the shop does not stock. Every trade emits store-transaction with the resulting balance. UI: the Survival card gained a fourth pane (Store) in ui/index.html, ui/styles.css and ui/js/survival.js - the tab badge carries the wallet, the pane draws GET /store grouped by category (icon, own N, buy/sell prices, unaffordable rows dimmed), Qty 1-99 plus Buy/Sell are real POST /store/buy and /store/sell, renderStore/syncStoreButtons keep the buttons honest, and a store-transaction frame repaints the shelf and the bag; the trade reply carries the balance but not the new owned counts, so trade() re-reads both /store and /inventory. Docs: API.md gained the three route sections (tables plus request/response bodies) and the wallet in the GET /survival sample, ARCHITECTURE.md a 'Store & economy' subsection plus the routes in the plugin endpoint list and the four-tab card, README.md the store.rs tree entry and an 'economy loop' highlight. Verified: cargo test --lib 142 passed (16 new) with 0 warnings, build-plugin.sh produced plugins/survival.wasm (337 KB), python tools/verify_docs.py exit 0, live API: GET /store answered 5 entries with coins 100, buy 3 worm_bait -> 88 coins and 8 bait, sell 2 driftwood -> 94 coins, refusals 409 (rods x2: required 150 shortfall 56; oversell: held 0) and 400 (count 0, unknown id), /context showed both store-transaction frames, OPTIONS preflight on /store/buy carried access-control-allow-origin: *, and the UI was driven in a real browser and in the shipped WebView over CDP: the Store tab rendered 5 rows / 3 headings with wallet 100, Sell 1 driftwood -> 'Sold 1 x Driftwood for 3 coins - 103 left' with wallet, badge and owned all moving to 103, buy 2 rods disabled Buy with 'costs 150, the purse holds 94', the list measured 252 px with no scrollbar, and a curl-side POST /store/buy repainted the pane to 79 coins with no click.

survival_cooking_from_bag.desc: Cooking now spends ingredients out of the bag, and the shop sells them. inventory.rs: a new ItemKind::Ingredient (so the bag's groups, the combination picker and the shop shelf all agree) plus the eight pantry items every recipe names - apple, egg, cheese, tomato, mushroom, noodles, bread, honey - each stack_max 12 (honey 8), food: Some(<same id>) so they are still edible raw. store.rs: StoreCategory::Ingredient + the same eight entries on the ingredients shelf at 3-8 coins buy / 1-3 sell (an omelette costs 11), so the catalog is 13 entries over four shelves; a new test walks model::RECIPES and fails if any ingredient is not stocked or any stocked ingredient is dead stock. plugin.rs: cook() checks missing_for(recipe) BEFORE eating, so a short pantry is a 409 missing_ingredients with {item,label,need,held,short} per line and costs nothing; the ingredients are removed only after the meal was accepted (a 409 too_full/still_digesting consumes nothing either), each removal emits inventory-changed with source: cook, and the reply gained a consumed array; recipes_json() folds the bag into the book (per-line held, can_cook, missing) and now backs both GET /recipes and the recipes array inside GET /foods. routes.rs uses recipes_json for those two routes. UI (ui/js/survival.js): renderRecipes shows the shortfall in the option text and tooltip, syncCraftButton disables Craft until can_cook (title names what is missing and points at the Store tab), the cook note prints what left the pantry (used 2 x Egg, 1 x Cheese), the Status feed picker shows own N per ingredient, and trade()/craft()/inventory-changed/store-transaction re-read the recipe book so cookability follows the bag without SSE. Docs: API.md gained the missing_ingredients body, the consumed array, the can_cook/missing/held recipe shape, the ingredient kind, the 13-entry/4-shelf store and corrected /foods counts; ARCHITECTURE.md the paid-cooking paragraph, the pantry in the store catalog, a fourth store invariant (every recipe ingredient stocked, no dead stock), the honest Cook row and the four-shelf store tab; README.md the pantry and the cooking loop. Verified: cargo test --lib 149 passed (7 new) with 0 warnings; build-plugin.sh -> plugins/survival.wasm 347 KB; verify_docs.py exit 0. Live API: /store answered 13 entries over bait/ingredient/material/tool with the starter bag, /recipes reported every recipe can_cook false with its full missing list, POST /survival/craft {omelette} answered 409 'cannot cook Cheese omelette - still need 2 x Egg, 1 x Cheese', buying 2 eggs + 1 cheese (6 + 5 coins) flipped can_cook true, and the cook then answered 200 with hunger 40 -> 66, consumed 2 Egg + 1 Cheese and a bag back to rod/bait/driftwood. Driven in a real browser and in the shipped WebView over CDP: the Store tab drew 13 rows under Bait/Ingredients/Materials/Tools (scrolling), the Cook row read 'Eggx2 (own 0) + Cheese (own 0) missing' with Craft disabled, buying the pair enabled it, and clicking Craft printed 'Cheese omelette eaten (+26 hunger) - hungry to peckish - well fed 4m - used 2 x Egg, 1 x Cheese' with the bag badge back to 3/20 and the row disabled again.

settings_nested_sections.desc: Bug: the Settings modal refused every save with 'no plugin owns `fishing` (known sections: tts, stt, vision, ai, survival)'. ui/js/settings.js addressed the two nested survival blocks as if they were top-level sections: `section: "fishing"` / `section: "inventory"` instead of `survival.fishing.*` / `survival.inventory.*`. renderSettings therefore read config.fishing (undefined), painted every fishing input blank, and — because a bool reads `value !== false` — showed enabled/require_rod/bait_required as checked; collectPatch then diffed those against nothing and posted {"fishing": {...}} to POST /config, which the host rejects because no plugin claims it. The bug shipped in 797676d (the fishing/inventory settings panes) and reproduced on the pre-fix binary: dirty 1 with patch {fishing:{enabled,hook_key,reel_key,require_rod,bait_required}} and the exact error text on Save. Fix: every survival field now addresses section `survival` with a dotted key (fishing.enabled, fishing.hook_key, ..., inventory.slots) so render/patch agree with watcher_rules.json, and the pane keeps its three cards via a new `group` property (buildForm filters on it instead of on the config section). Guard: tools/verify_docs.py gained check 6 — it collects the sections POST /config owns (tts, stt, vision, ai plus every plugins/*/src/config.rs CONFIG_KEY = survival) and fails on any FIELDS section outside that set; verified by reintroducing `section: "fishing"` (exit 1, 'fishing.fishing.hook_key addresses a section POST /config does not own'), then reverting. Verified in the shipped WebView over CDP: after rebuilding, Settings opens with dirty 0 and real values (hook_key Space, reel_key Space, difficulty 1, min_wait 3, hook_window 1400, sweet_width 0.22, bag slots 20, hunger drain 1.5); editing difficulty to 1.5 produced patch {survival:{fishing:{difficulty:1.5}}} and saved 'saved 1 change(s) · applied live' with GET /survival's config.fishing.difficulty at 1.5; setting it back to 1 saved again and left watcher_rules.json byte-identical to HEAD (the .bak was removed). Same flow screenshotted in a plain browser with the Fishing card fully populated. verify_docs.py exit 0 with 38 fields over tts/stt/vision/survival.
